note: Devi Bhagavata, Skandha 7: Hindi put back on the verse it belongs to, matched by Sanskrit content and the printed numbering. The Hindi is the printed Gita Press translation with mechanical clean-up only; where the edition groups verses, the paragraph is shown once on the first verse (hindiRange) and the others point to it (hindiSeeVerse). Every entry is in data/ocr-hindi-review.json under this queue and is withheld until proofread against the printed page.

source.edition: Gita Press Gorakhpur, श्रीमद्देवीभागवतमहापुराण (सचित्र, सरल हिन्दी-व्याख्यासहित), 2 खण्ड
source.text: Two independent readings of volume 2: (1) Tesseract 5.4 OCR (hin model) of the local scan "Devi Bhagavt Puran of Veda Vyas with Hindi Explanation and Illustration - Gita Press.pdf" (volume 2, 888 pages), each page read at two independently found column cuts and once whole; (2) archive.org item "21-devi-bhagavata-with-hindi-translation-vol-1-gitapress-2010": the OCR text of the edition ("… Vol 2 (Gitapress) 2010_djvu.txt", 6,000,980 bytes), downloaded with the owner's approval on 2026-10-27, kept locally in scripts/cache/devibhagavat-gitapress-2010/, not committed.

guards: Sanskrit 3-gram Jaccard >= 0.6 and >= 0.15 above the next printed verse
printed adhyaya (between two consecutive Sanskrit colophons; skandha named in the colophon or the running heads) agrees with the verse
printed Sanskrit verse number agrees with the verse
the Hindi paragraph is printed beside it, closes with its own "॥ n ॥", its printed number covers the verse, and the paragraph before it ends exactly on the verse before (no half verses)
a range covers at most 5 verses, every one passes the Sanskrit and number guards, and they are consecutive in the library
the library verse holds a single printed verse
no line of the paragraph was dropped or left unclassified as unreadable, and it does not open with a stray letter
no page number, running head, colophon or heading left after mechanical clean-up (ASCII digits, page specks, avagraha and visarga glyphs)
a single: the Hindi shares at least 2 more word stems with its own verse than with any verse 1-3 places away; a range: at least 3 stems and 2 more than the neighbouring range of the same length

a verse from the scan is kept only where archive.org's text printed the same paragraph (same adhyaya and numbers) with >= 0.8 letter-trigram similarity; the scan paragraph itself also agreed across both column cuts and with the whole-page reading at every line start and end
a verse that only archive.org's text passed (the scan had lost it to OCR damage) passes every guard above on that text alone
where both readings passed but differ, or group the verses differently, the verse is left out
